analysis: Reviewed the supplied base text of .github/workflows/release-provider.yml (lines 550-1496) plus the patch excerpt. The changes are: runs-on blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404 to ubuntu-24.04 for resolve-env (line 135), a qualification job (line 304), stage-release (1210) and publish-release (1319), and a new timeout-minutes: 90 on the macOS signing job (head 343). The signing job stays on blacksmith-12vcpu-macos-27. Its Developer ID import, signing, keychain removal, notarization, stapling and final-bytes verification are unchanged, as are the exact-artifact digest download and the publication scripts. The only security-relevant effect is that jobs holding R2 credentials and RELEASE_KEY (A-005, A-011 registry) now run on GitHub-hosted runners. Permissions remain least-privilege (contents: write only in publish-release), persist-credentials is false, actions are pinned by SHA, and tools install with --require-hashes. Hosted runners are ephemeral, so no concrete regression was shown. The 90-minute timeout reduces the hung-job exposure of the signing keychain and is benign. Limits: the patch excerpt is truncated and the head text was not supplied, so I could not confirm whether the line 135 job (resolve-env) and the line 304 job handle any secrets. The mapping of runner pools to the trust boundary lives outside the supplied evidence, so this is raised as low severity only.

findings.detail: The patch changes runs-on for stage-release (base line 1210) and publish-release (base line 1319, head 1320) from blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404 to ubuntu-24.04, and the same swap applies to resolve-env and a qualification job. Those jobs resolve and use R2 write credentials and the coordinator RELEASE_KEY (A-005), then register hashes in the provider binary hash registry (A-011). The workflow's own comment says to "keep the older-OS proof within the release trust boundary", so runner placement is treated as a boundary. The jobs still take secrets only after hash-pinned tool installation and use pinned actions, so no concrete exploit is shown. The runner trust and isolation change is undocumented and the threat model does not say which runner pools may hold release credentials. Fix: record in the threat model or workflow that GitHub-hosted runners are accepted for these jobs, or keep them on the prior pool.
findings.title: Release publication jobs holding R2 and release-key secrets moved from Blacksmith to GitHub-hosted runners
